prompt: According to the lesson, why is a plain-markdown-plus-git knowledge base a legitimate choice for a Learning OS, instead of requiring an app like Obsidian?
choices: It's the only option that works offline
It stores notes as plain files you version, search, and back up with git, a tool you already know, with no new app lock-in
It automatically generates backlinks between notes
It's required by most employers before hiring

prompt: In the dev journal format shown in the lesson, what is the specific purpose of the "What I'll remember" line?
choices: It restates the error message verbatim so it's easier to search for
It lists which files were changed in the fix
It summarizes the one takeaway that would have saved time if you'd known it before debugging
It's optional filler that's rarely filled in

prompt: In the lesson's example, a January note about a CORS preflight fix and a June note about a missing WebSocket cookie are both tagged #cors. What actually made that shared tag valuable five months later?
choices: The tag automatically fixed the June bug without any reading required
Searching the tag surfaced the January note, which already explained the Access-Control-Allow-Credentials requirement, cutting debugging time
It let the note-taking tool auto-delete the duplicate note
It proved the January note's root cause was wrong

prompt: What is the core argument in the lesson's before/after scenario comparing re-debugging from scratch to reusing an old note?
choices: Re-debugging from scratch is always faster because you double-check your own reasoning
Writing notes is wasted time since most bugs never recur
The small time spent writing a note once is repaid every time the same class of bug resurfaces, because searching beats re-deriving
Notes should be deleted as soon as the bug they describe is fixed

prompt: Why does the lesson stress using a consistent tag spelling (e.g., always #cors) instead of inventing a new variant each time (#corsissue, #cors-bug, #corsstuff)?
choices: Note-taking tools require a fixed tag list to be registered in advance
Inconsistent tags fragment your search, so a future matching problem won't surface your past notes
Git rejects commits containing more than one tag spelling
Tags longer than 10 characters break markdown rendering

prompt: The journal format records "Context" and "Symptom" as separate fields from "Root cause." What is the stated reason for that separation?
choices: So future-you, or a search, can match a new bug to an old one by what was observed, even before knowing the cause is related
Markdown requires distinct headers for each paragraph for grammatical correctness
Context is meant for an employer to read; root cause is meant to stay private
They are interchangeable, so only one of the two ever needs to be filled in
